content: To utilize this approach, we need to efficiently optimize the log marginal likelihood of observed sentences. While compound PCFGs break efficient inference, if the latent vector is known the distribution over trees reduces to a standard PCFG. This property allows us to perform grammar induction using a collapsed approach where the latent trees are marginalized out exactly with dynamic programming. To handle the latent vector, we employ standard amortized inference using reparameterized samples from a variational posterior approximated from an inference network BIBREF12 , BIBREF13 .
